section_summary: This section records Japanese efforts to secure petroleum and oil equipment, American companies’ dealings with Japanese buyers, and State Department discussions of export controls. It includes correspondence on particular shipments, an extended report on Japan’s motor fuel shortages and substitute fuels, and a memorandum proposing quotas on American petroleum exports. Several pages are duplicate copies or cross-reference notes.

people.name: John Hickerson
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of European Affairs

people.name: Mr. Fitch
people.role: official whose inquiry prompted shipment reports

people.name: S. C. Wollmar
people.role: vice-president and treasurer of Davis and Company

people.name: H. M. van Bommelen
people.role: translator of the motor fuel report

people.name: W. H. Pinckard
people.role: vice president, California Texas Oil Company

subfiles.title: Purchase of American oil on credit by Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a report that Japanese attempts to buy American oil on credit were unsuccessful.
subfiles.summary: References Naval Attaché Report No. 100.

subfiles.title: Japanese inquiry for lubricating oil outside export restrictions
subfiles.about: Records Standard-Vacuum’s inquiry about supplying lubricating oil that could be reworked for aircraft engines.
subfiles.summary: Leaper described a proposed sale of 50,000 drums that fell outside the July 26 licensing definition. Yost said no restriction currently applied and forwarded the facts to the Export Control Administrator.

subfiles.title: Copy of memorandum on Japanese lubricating-oil inquiry
subfiles.about: Duplicates the memorandum on a proposed Japanese purchase of lubricating oil outside current controls.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the August 27 memorandum concerning 50,000 drums of potentially aircraft-suitable lubricating oil.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing cable on Japanese crude-oil negotiations
subfiles.about: Transmits the cable Walden sent about Japanese crude-oil requirements.
subfiles.summary: Walden says the enclosed cable matches the substance of his earlier discussion with Hornbeck.

subfiles.title: Cable on Talang Akar crude for Japanese requirements
subfiles.about: Offers Talang Akar crude through alternative arrangements and asks about importing replacement crude for refining.
subfiles.summary: Walden reports no available aviation gasoline and asks whether crude from elsewhere could enter in bond for refining and re-export.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden’s crude-oil cable
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Walden’s letter and cable.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Walden for supplying the August 23 cable.

subfiles.title: Japanese petroleum activities in Mexico
subfiles.about: Points to reporting on Japanese businessmen and petroleum interests around Tampico, Veracruz, and the isthmus.
subfiles.summary: References despatch No. 11428 and its enclosures.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Connally on gasoline exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Explains which gasoline shipments to Japan were subject to the July 1940 export restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Hull says the restrictions cover aviation motor fuel as defined by regulation and that licenses cover only types unused by American armed forces.

subfiles.title: Senate referral of Bowden’s telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards a constituent’s telegram for consideration and a report.
subfiles.summary: Requests a report to accompany return of the enclosure.

subfiles.title: Telegram questioning a gasoline shipment to Japan
subfiles.about: Questions why a ship loading gasoline in drums at Texas City was exempt from the embargo.
subfiles.summary: Bowden alleges the gasoline was listed as general cargo for Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Sheppard on reported oil shipment
subfiles.about: Responds to a report that a million tons of oil had been approved for shipment to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains that restrictions covered aviation gasoline and lubricants, while other petroleum products remained unrestricted.

subfiles.title: Sheppard’s inquiry about oil shipment approval
subfiles.about: Forwards Dickson’s letter and asks whether the reported oil shipment was approved.
subfiles.summary: Sheppard requests an answer to his constituent’s allegation.

subfiles.title: Dickson’s letter about reported million-ton oil shipment
subfiles.about: Seeks clarification of a magazine claim that the United States approved a million-ton oil shipment to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dickson urges Sheppard to investigate the claim or correct the public record.

subfiles.title: Forced sale of American shares in Bitumuls Company
subfiles.about: Reports pressure to sell American-held Bitumuls shares and refusal of a foreign-exchange permit.
subfiles.summary: Grew says he made informal representations to Japan’s foreign minister.

subfiles.title: British Embassy information on aviation-gasoline sales
subfiles.about: Records British Embassy reports of two planned 87-octane gasoline cargoes from New Orleans to a Japanese company.
subfiles.summary: Helm identified the vessels, drum quantities, seller, buyer, and reported prices.

subfiles.title: Supplementary report on Davis and Company oil shipment
subfiles.about: Identifies the broker that asked Davis and Company to ship oil to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wollmar said Damex Engineering of Mexico City arranged the shipment but did not identify its underlying buyer.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Davis and Company oil shipment
subfiles.about: Investigates the route, consignee, payment, and corporate background of an oil cargo sent to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The report identifies low-grade Mexican oil loaded at New Orleans, redirected from Osaka to Yura, and paid through a New York letter of credit arranged from Switzerland. It disputes earlier claims about Tenerife and German financing and describes W. R. Davis’s business background.

subfiles.title: Copy of investigation of Davis and Company oil shipment
subfiles.about: Duplicates the investigation of Davis and Company’s oil cargo to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The copy traces Mexican oil from New Orleans to Yura and describes the consignee, financing, and Davis companies. It repeats denials of Tenerife routing and German involvement.

subfiles.title: Departmental discussion of Japanese Army gasoline inquiry
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Standard-Vacuum’s response to a Japanese Army gasoline inquiry in China.
subfiles.summary: Officers raised no objection; Hornbeck questioned the proposed one-year term, which the company said it would shorten.

subfiles.title: Shanghai cable on Japanese Army gasoline requirements
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese Army inquiry for gasoline in Shanghai, Canton, and Tientsin.
subfiles.summary: The cable gives quantities, payment terms, and a stated civilian transport use.

subfiles.title: Walden’s report on Japanese oil purchases and tanker shortage
subfiles.about: Relays reports on Japanese oil orders, tanker constraints, and California shipments.
subfiles.summary: Walden says Japan still had substantial American oil and gasoline on order but lacked tanker and cargo space to lift more. He supplies August 1940 California shipment figures by company and product.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden’s shipment report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Walden’s information from California.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Walden for his October 24 letter.

subfiles.title: Oil situation in Japan and German-controlled territory
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum and review on oil supplies in Japan and German-controlled territory.
subfiles.summary: References a Treasury Department letter.

subfiles.title: Japanese interest in oil-well drilling equipment
subfiles.about: Points to Walden’s letter on drilling machinery sought for the Dutch East Indies.
subfiles.summary: References a State Department memorandum and enclosure.

subfiles.title: File note on previously reported matter
subfiles.about: Notes that a matter had already been reported by telegram.
subfiles.summary: The remaining handwriting is too unclear to identify the matter.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Bitumuls correspondence
subfiles.about: Transmits records of Grew’s representations about the proposed sale of American Bitumuls shares.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a conversation memorandum and the oral representations left with Japan’s foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Grew’s conversation with Matsuoka about Bitumuls
subfiles.about: Records informal representations concerning forced sale of American majority shares in Bitumuls.
subfiles.summary: Grew raised the companies’ position with Japan’s foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Oral representations on Bitumuls share sale
subfiles.about: Sets out American shareholdings and the denied permit to convert sale proceeds into foreign exchange.
subfiles.summary: Details the 7,466 American-held shares and the October 30 permit refusal.

subfiles.title: Socony-Vacuum tender for Colombian crude
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on Mitsui’s invitation for Socony-Vacuum to supply Colombian crude oil.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Department had no objection to the proposed supply.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting report on Japanese motor fuel
subfiles.about: Transmits a translated Netherlands consular report on Japan’s motor fuel problems.
subfiles.summary: Foote says a local oil-company director regarded the report as reliable.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Motor Fuel Problem
subfiles.from: J. I. D. Pennink, Netherlands consul general at Kobe
subfiles.about: Surveys Japan’s oil imports, refining limits, substitute fuels, synthetic-fuel plans, and military needs.
subfiles.summary: Pennink argues that Japan depended heavily on imported petroleum, especially for aviation gasoline, despite rationing and efforts to make alcohol, charcoal gas, and synthetic fuel. The report reviews distribution controls, refinery construction, coal constraints, foreign-exchange difficulties, and prospective oil sources in East Asia and Mexico. It concludes that Japanese fuel self-sufficiency remained distant.

subfiles.title: File reference to another oil record
subfiles.about: Directs the reader to another decimal-file record.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten reference: see 894.24/1235.

subfiles.title: Walden’s letter enclosing California shipment figures
subfiles.about: Sends Hornbeck information received from California.
subfiles.summary: Walden encloses figures on petroleum shipments to Japan.

subfiles.title: California petroleum shipments to Japan, November 1940
subfiles.about: Lists November shipments by oil company and product category.
subfiles.summary: Reports nearly 2.2 million barrels shipped, including crude sent to Dairen.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Walden’s shipment statistics
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Walden’s January 27 letter and California petroleum statistics.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Walden for the shipment figures.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japan’s petroleum stocks and tanker deliveries
subfiles.about: Records discussion with Standard-Vacuum executives about Japanese oil quotas and tanker availability.
subfiles.summary: Walden and Parker discussed how to answer a Japanese offer affecting oil imports and distribution. Hornbeck suggested accepting while recognizing that scarce tankers could delay or prevent deliveries; they agreed to pursue that approach with Shell.

subfiles.title: Indexing note on Morishima conversation
subfiles.about: Notes that a conversation memorandum involving Morishima had not yet been indexed.
subfiles.summary: Administrative indexing note.

subfiles.title: Morishima’s proposed compromise in gasoline-company lawsuit
subfiles.about: Records Morishima’s report of a proposed settlement between Japan Gasoline and Universal Oil Products.
subfiles.summary: The dispute arose after Universal declined to perform a 1938 contract under the moral embargo policy. Morishima said lawyers would discuss a compromise and asked Green to inform Berle.

subfiles.title: Copy of Morishima conversation memorandum
subfiles.about: Duplicates the memorandum on a proposed compromise in the Japan Gasoline–Universal dispute.
subfiles.summary: Repeats Morishima’s account of settlement talks and possible submission of an agreement to the Department.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Morishima conversation memorandum
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the memorandum on the Japan Gasoline–Universal dispute.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the proposed compromise and Morishima’s request to inform Berle.

subfiles.title: Pinckard’s report on naval fuel inquiries and China trade restrictions
subfiles.about: Reports inquiries for Japanese and French naval fuel and restrictions on foreign kerosene sales in China.
subfiles.summary: Pinckard says his company declined to quote on fuel-oil inquiries. Reports from several Chinese cities describe Japanese military limits on foreign kerosene imports, transport, and sales.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Pinckard’s letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Pinckard’s information on fuel inquiries and China operations.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Pinckard for confirming their telephone discussion and supplying additional reports.

subfiles.title: Japanese interest in Peruvian petroleum
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch investigating reports of Japanese interest in Peruvian oil fields.
subfiles.summary: Notes that company and ministry contacts knew of no such survey.

subfiles.title: Fusel-oil shipments from the United States to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on sharply increased American shipments of fusel oil and other alcohols to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Compares 1940 shipments with lower totals in 1939 and 1938.

subfiles.title: Oil supplies to Japan
subfiles.about: Points to material on shipments of oil and other raw materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The source details are largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Petroleum stocks in Thailand
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on Thai petroleum stocks potentially useful in a Japanese drive toward Singapore.
subfiles.summary: Also references shipment of petroleum in containers under thirty gallons.

subfiles.title: Covering note on Japan’s petroleum supplies
subfiles.about: Draws attention to Japan’s supplies of lubricating oil, crude oil, and gasoline.
subfiles.summary: A poorly legible note appears to enclose related material.

subfiles.title: Limitation of Petroleum Exports to Japan
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Proposes category-specific quotas to curb Japan’s growing purchases of American petroleum products.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum links the sharp rise in Japanese gasoline and lubricant purchases to war preparation and stock building. It recommends quarterly export quotas based on 1936 shipments, with incremental allowance for ordinary growth and exceptions for selected countries. Historical tables compare crude oil, fuel oil, lubricants, greases, and gasoline exports through 1940. The document continues beyond page 160.
